questions.explanation: Mothballs change directly from solid to gas, slowly shrinking - this is sublimation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Particles in a liquid are ____ compared to particles in a solid.
choices: Able to slide past one another
Completely far apart like a gas
questions.answer: Able to slide past one another
questions.explanation: Liquid particles are close together but not locked in place, so they can slide past one another and flow.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement about solids is TRUE?
choices: Solid particles vibrate in fixed positions
Solids take the shape of their container
questions.answer: Solid particles vibrate in fixed positions
questions.explanation: Solid particles cannot travel around; they only vibrate while staying in place, giving solids a fixed shape.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Cooking oil poured from a bottle into a pan shows that liquids ____.
choices: Take the shape of the container
questions.answer: Take the shape of the container
questions.explanation: The oil flows and adopts the shape of the pan while keeping the same volume - classic liquid behavior.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement about liquids is TRUE?
questions.answer: Liquids can flow
questions.explanation: Liquids flow and can be poured because their particles can slide past one another.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A substance with particles that are close together but free to move around is most likely a ____.
questions.answer: Liquid
questions.explanation: Liquids have particles close together yet free to move - between the fixed particles of solids and the far-apart particles of gases.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the main difference between evaporation and boiling?
choices: Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature while boiling happens throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature
Boiling happens only at the surface
They are exactly the same process
Evaporation happens only in the freezer
questions.answer: Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature while boiling happens throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a slow surface process at any temperature; boiling is rapid vapor formation throughout the liquid at its boiling point.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Water droplets forming on the outside of a cold glass show which process?
questions.answer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Water vapor in the air cools on the cold surface and changes into liquid droplets - condensation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of these is an example of a gas?
questions.answer: Oxygen
questions.explanation: Oxygen spreads out to fill any container, which is the behavior of a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: What is the process called when a liquid changes into a gas?
questions.answer: Evaporation
questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs when liquid particles gain enough energy to escape into the air as gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Which state of matter takes the shape of its container but keeps a definite volume?
questions.answer: Liquid
questions.explanation: Liquids flow to match the shape of their container, yet their volume stays constant.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: Frost forming on cold windows on a chilly morning involves water vapor changing into ____.
questions.answer: Solid ice crystals
questions.explanation: When water vapor loses enough heat on a very cold surface, it can form solid ice crystals (frost).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: When you squeeze a sponge filled with air, the air inside can be compressed because ____.
choices: Gas particles have large spaces between them
questions.answer: Gas particles have large spaces between them
questions.explanation: The spaces between gas particles allow gases to be compressed into a smaller volume.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which observation BEST shows that air is matter in the gas state?
choices: An inflated balloon weighs slightly more than a deflated one
questions.answer: An inflated balloon weighs slightly more than a deflated one
questions.explanation: Air has mass and takes up space - the inflated balloon is slightly heavier because it contains compressed gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a state of matter discussed in this lesson?
questions.answer: Energy
questions.explanation: Solid, liquid, and gas are states of matter; energy is not a state of matter.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A spinning top on the floor shows mainly ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: A spinning top turns rapidly around its own axis while staying nearly in one place.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: A car moving straight along a highway is an example of ____.
choices: Circular motion of the whole car
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: The whole car moves from one place to another in the same direction - translational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Gears inside a mechanical watch mainly show ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: Each gear spins around its own axle, transferring motion to other gears.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Which type of motion is mainly responsible for day and night?
questions.answer: Rotational motion of the Earth
questions.explanation: Earth's rotation on its axis makes different sides face the Sun, producing day and night.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: When you push a box straight across the floor, the box undergoes ____.
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: Every part of the box moves the same distance in the same direction - translation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Which statement correctly contrasts translational and rotational motion?
choices: Translation always moves objects in circles
Rotation moves objects in straight lines
Translation moves the whole object along a path while rotation turns it around an axis
questions.answer: Translation moves the whole object along a path while rotation turns it around an axis
questions.explanation: Translation shifts an object along a path; rotation spins it about an axis.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: An elevator moving up inside a building shows ____.
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: The whole elevator cab moves straight up (or down) - translational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: The blades of a helicopter lifting off vertically spin to create lift. The blades show ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: The blades spin around the helicopter's central rotor axis - rotational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: When a door swings open on its hinges, the door shows ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion around the hinges
questions.explanation: Every point on the door moves in an arc around the hinge line - rotation around the hinges.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches the object and its motion?
choices: Train on a straight track - rotational
questions.answer: Ceiling fan - rotational
questions.explanation: A ceiling fan spins around its axis (rotational); a straight-moving train and elevator are translational examples.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: A satellite dish slowly turning to face a satellite shows ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: The dish rotates around its mount to track the satellite.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which example shows translational motion in a curved path?
choices: A car driving along a curved road
questions.answer: A car driving along a curved road
questions.explanation: The whole car still moves along the road (translation), even though the path is curved; the car itself is not spinning.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: A skier gliding straight downhill without turning demonstrates ____.
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: The skier moves as a whole in one direction down the slope - translational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: A Ferris wheel turning slowly is an example of ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: The wheel rotates around its central axle - rotational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A conveyor belt carrying boxes in a straight line is an example of ____.
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: The boxes travel in one straight direction with the belt - translational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A confined fluid at 100 Pa pushes on a piston of area 3 m2. What force results?
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 100 Pa x 3 m2 = 300 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: A hydraulic system has input piston area 2 m2 and output piston area 8 m2. The force multiplication is ____.
questions.answer: 4 times
questions.explanation: Force multiplication equals the area ratio: 8 / 2 = 4, so output force is 4 times the input force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which is TRUE about the pressure at the input and output pistons of an ideal hydraulic lift?
choices: Pressure is higher at the input
The pressure is the same at both pistons
Pressure is higher at the output
Pressure is zero at the output
questions.answer: The pressure is the same at both pistons
questions.explanation: Pascal's Principle transmits the pressure undiminished, so both pistons experience the same pressure.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: If you squeeze a filled, sealed plastic water bottle at the middle, the pressure inside ____.
questions.answer: Increases equally throughout the water
questions.explanation: Squeezing adds pressure to the confined water, and Pascal's Principle says it spreads equally in all directions.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A force of 50 N produces a pressure of 10 Pa. What area is the force applied to?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A nurse presses a syringe plunger and fluid comes out the needle. This best illustrates ____.
choices: Pressure in a confined fluid pushing fluid out through an opening
questions.answer: Pressure in a confined fluid pushing fluid out through an opening
questions.explanation: Pressing the plunger raises pressure inside the confined fluid, forcing it out through the narrow needle.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A confined fluid at 20 Pa pushes on a piston of area 8 m2. What force results?
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 20 Pa x 8 m2 = 160 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Why are hydraulic systems filled with liquid rather than gas for lifting heavy loads?
choices: Liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure transfers efficiently
questions.answer: Liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure transfers efficiently
questions.explanation: Liquids barely compress, so nearly all applied pressure is transmitted to do work; gases would compress and absorb much of it.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: A force of 20 N is applied over an area of 4 m2. What is the pressure?
questions.answer: 5 Pa
questions.explanation: P = F / A = 20 N / 4 m2 = 5 Pa (pascals).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: If 300 N is applied to a piston with area 0.5 m2, the pressure created is ____.
questions.answer: 600 Pa
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: In a hydraulic system, a small force on a small piston can lift a heavy load on a large piston because ____.
choices: Pressure is transmitted equally, so the larger piston area produces a larger force
Gravity is reduced inside the system
questions.answer: Pressure is transmitted equally, so the larger piston area produces a larger force
questions.explanation: Equal pressure on a larger area means a larger output force: F2 = P x A2. This is how force is multiplied.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 40 N produces a pressure of 20 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of these is NOT an application of Pascal's Principle?
choices: A balloon floating upward in air
questions.answer: A balloon floating upward in air
questions.explanation: A rising balloon relies on buoyancy (Archimedes), not on transmitted fluid pressure in a confined system.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: A force of 180 N produces a pressure of 10 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Which fluid property makes Pascal's Principle work well in hydraulics?
questions.answer: Incompressibility of liquids
questions.explanation: Because liquids barely compress, applied pressure is transmitted almost completely through the system.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Car lifts in repair shops raise vehicles using ____.
choices: Hydraulic systems based on Pascal's Principle
questions.answer: Hydraulic systems based on Pascal's Principle
questions.explanation: Hydraulic lifts use confined fluid pressure to multiply a small input force into a large lifting force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Doubling the area over which the same force acts will ____ the pressure.
questions.answer: Halve
questions.explanation: Since P = F / A, spreading the same force over twice the area halves the pressure.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A sharp knife cuts easily because the thin edge ____.
choices: Concentrates force on a very small area, creating high pressure
questions.answer: Concentrates force on a very small area, creating high pressure
questions.explanation: The same push over a tiny edge area produces very high pressure, so the knife cuts easily.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 120 N produces a pressure of 10 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: The 'confined' requirement in Pascal's Principle means the fluid must be ____.
questions.answer: Enclosed in a sealed system
questions.explanation: The fluid must be enclosed so the applied pressure cannot escape and is transmitted through the whole fluid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: According to legend, Archimedes used his principle to check whether a crown was ____.
choices: Pure gold or mixed with cheaper metal
questions.answer: Pure gold or mixed with cheaper metal
questions.explanation: By comparing water displacement of the crown with equal weights of pure gold, Archimedes could detect lighter mixed metals.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Dead Sea swimmers float very easily because the water ____.
questions.answer: Is extremely salty and dense
questions.explanation: Very high salt content makes Dead Sea water dense, producing a large buoyant force that keeps swimmers high on the surface.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A submarine surfaces by ____.
choices: Pumping water out of its ballast tanks to become lighter
questions.answer: Pumping water out of its ballast tanks to become lighter
questions.explanation: Expelling ballast water reduces weight below the buoyant force, so the submarine rises.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Objects denser than water generally ____.
questions.answer: Sink
questions.explanation: If an object's density exceeds water's, its weight beats the buoyant force, so it sinks.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: The apparent weight of an object underwater is ____ its true weight in air.
questions.answer: Less than
questions.explanation: Buoyant force partially supports the object, so its measured (apparent) weight underwater is less.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A ship's 'displacement' rating refers to ____.
choices: The weight of water the hull displaces
questions.answer: The weight of water the hull displaces
questions.explanation: Naval displacement measures the weight of water displaced by the ship, equal to the ship's total weight when floating.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: Objects less dense than water generally ____.
questions.answer: Float
questions.explanation: Lower density than water means buoyant force can balance the object's weight, so it floats.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: An object sinks when its weight is ____ the maximum buoyant force.
questions.answer: Greater than
questions.explanation: If weight exceeds the buoyant force from the displaced fluid, the object sinks.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Buoyant force on a fully submerged object depends on ____.
choices: The object's color and shape only
How deep it is pushed (beyond full submersion)
The fluid's density and the object's volume
questions.answer: The fluid's density and the object's volume
questions.explanation: Once fully submerged, buoyant force = fluid density x displaced volume x gravity - depth alone changes nothing.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A submerged object feels lighter because ____.
choices: Buoyant force pushes up against its weight
questions.answer: Buoyant force pushes up against its weight
questions.explanation: The upward buoyant force offsets part of the object's weight.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: If an object displaces 8 N of water and weighs 8 N, it will ____.
choices: Rise out of the water completely
questions.answer: Float (remain balanced in the water)
questions.explanation: Buoyant force equals weight, so the object is balanced - it floats without sinking or rising further.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: Which ancient scientist is Archimedes' Principle named after?
questions.answer: Archimedes of Syracuse
questions.explanation: Archimedes of Syracuse, a Greek mathematician, discovered the principle of buoyancy.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: A duck floats easily on a lake mainly because ____.
choices: Its body displaces enough water and air trapped in feathers adds buoyancy
questions.answer: Its body displaces enough water and air trapped in feathers adds buoyancy
questions.explanation: The duck's shape and air-trapping feathers increase displaced volume, giving strong buoyant force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Why does a steel ship float even though steel sinks in water?
choices: The ship's shape displaces a large volume of water, creating enough buoyant force
questions.answer: The ship's shape displaces a large volume of water, creating enough buoyant force
questions.explanation: The hollow hull displaces a huge amount of water; the weight of that displaced water equals or exceeds the ship's weight, so it floats.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Archimedes' Principle applies to ____.
questions.answer: Both liquids and gases
questions.explanation: Buoyancy occurs in all fluids - liquids and gases alike (ships in water, balloons in air).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Who is known as the 'Father of Medicine'?
questions.answer: Hippocrates
questions.explanation: Hippocrates of ancient Greece is called the Father of Medicine; doctors still take a version of his oath.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Who developed the germ theory of disease and pasteurization?
questions.answer: Louis Pasteur
questions.explanation: Louis Pasteur proved germs cause disease and created pasteurization to kill harmful microbes in food.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Which ancient Greek philosopher classified animals and laid early foundations of biology?
questions.answer: Aristotle
questions.explanation: Aristotle systematically observed and classified animals, influencing biology for centuries.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Who pioneered wireless radio communication over long distances?
questions.answer: Guglielmo Marconi
questions.explanation: Guglielmo Marconi developed practical long-distance radio telegraphy and won the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who invented the first mercury thermometer scale widely used in science?
choices: Lord Kelvin invented the first thermometer
Galileo invented the modern mercury scale
Anders Celsius only invented all scales
questions.answer: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit
questions.explanation: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit created the mercury thermometer and its scale in the early 1700s; Celsius and Kelvin scales came later.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Which scientist is famous for E = mc2?
questions.answer: Albert Einstein
questions.explanation: Einstein's mass-energy equivalence, E = mc2, is part of his special theory of relativity.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.answer: Charles Darwin
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed evolution by natural selection in his 1859 book On the Origin of Species.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity?
questions.answer: Albert Einstein
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein developed the special and general theories of relativity, transforming modern physics.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who created the first successful vaccine, against smallpox?
questions.answer: Edward Jenner
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796, the world's first successful vaccine.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who is famous for the laws of motion and universal gravitation?
questions.answer: Isaac Newton
questions.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton published the laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation in his 1687 work Principia.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Who discovered natural radioactivity in uranium?
questions.answer: Henri Becquerel
questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 when uranium salts fogged photographic plates.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: Who measured the speed of light accurately using rotating mirrors in the 1800s?
choices: Armand Fizeau and Leon Foucault refined such measurements
Isaac Newton measured it with candles only
Galileo measured it exactly with lanterns
questions.answer: Armand Fizeau and Leon Foucault refined such measurements
questions.explanation: Fizeau and Foucault used rotating toothed wheels and mirrors in the mid-1800s to measure light's speed accurately.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Who discovered the circulation of blood through the body?
questions.answer: William Harvey
questions.explanation: William Harvey described the full circulation of blood pumped by the heart in 1628.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who proposed continental drift, the idea that continents slowly move?
questions.answer: Alfred Wegener
questions.explanation: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912; plate tectonics later confirmed his idea.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Who proposed the quantum theory that energy comes in discrete packets (quanta)?
questions.answer: Max Planck
questions.explanation: Max Planck proposed in 1900 that energy is emitted in discrete packets called quanta, founding quantum theory.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Which state of matter has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume?
questions.answer: Gas
questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely and spread out to fill the entire container, so gases have no fixed shape or volume.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Which of these substances is in the liquid state at room temperature?
questions.answer: Alcohol
questions.explanation: At room temperature alcohol is a liquid, iron and sand are solids, and oxygen is a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: What happens to the particles of a substance when it is heated?
questions.answer: They move faster
questions.explanation: Heat adds energy to particles, making them vibrate or move faster, which can cause a change of state.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the three states of matter?
choices: Solids have the least particle energy and gases have the most
Liquids have more particle energy than gases
All three states have equal particle energy
Gases have the least particle energy
questions.answer: Solids have the least particle energy and gases have the most
questions.explanation: Particle energy increases from solid (least) to liquid to gas (most).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Particles of which state of matter have strong attraction that holds them in a fixed arrangement?
questions.answer: Solid
questions.explanation: Strong particle attraction in solids locks them into a fixed, orderly arrangement.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which state of matter is water at 120 degrees Celsius under normal pressure?
questions.answer: Gas
questions.explanation: Above 100 degrees Celsius (its boiling point at normal pressure), water exists as water vapor, a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Ice melting in a glass of juice is an example of which process?
questions.answer: Melting
questions.explanation: The warm juice transfers heat to the ice, so the solid ice changes into liquid water.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: Which change of state happens when wet clothes dry under the sun?
questions.answer: Liquid to gas
questions.explanation: Heat from the sun turns the liquid water in the clothes into water vapor, which escapes into the air.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Which of these is an example of a solid?
questions.answer: Ice cube
questions.explanation: An ice cube keeps its own shape and volume, which are the defining traits of a solid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: The smell of perfume spreading across a room shows that gas particles ____.
questions.answer: Move and spread out freely
questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely in all directions, so perfume particles diffuse through the air until the smell spreads.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: When water vapor in clouds turns into raindrops, the process is ____.
questions.answer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Water vapor (gas) cools in clouds and condenses into liquid water droplets that fall as rain.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of these is an example of a liquid?
questions.answer: Water
questions.explanation: Water flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping a fixed volume, so it is a liquid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: Steam from a hot cup of coffee is water in which state?
questions.answer: Gas
questions.explanation: Steam is water vapor - water in its gaseous state after gaining heat.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the process called when a solid changes into a liquid?
questions.answer: Melting
questions.explanation: Melting happens when a solid absorbs heat and its particles break free from fixed positions.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Water boiling in a kettle changes from which state to which state?
questions.answer: Liquid to gas
questions.explanation: Boiling gives liquid water enough energy to become water vapor, a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement about rotational motion is TRUE?
choices: Points near the axis move faster in a straight line
Points farther from the axis travel a larger circle
All points travel the same distance
questions.answer: Points farther from the axis travel a larger circle
questions.explanation: During rotation, points farther from the axis sweep out bigger circles than points near the axis.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A toy car travels 10 meters in 5 seconds. What is its average speed?
questions.answer: 2 meters per second
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 10 m / 5 s = 2 m/s.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which scenario shows an object in translational motion only?
choices: A sled sliding down a straight slope
questions.answer: A sled sliding down a straight slope
questions.explanation: The sled moves straight down the slope without spinning, so it shows translational motion only.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Which best describes the motion of a bullet train traveling on a straight rail?
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: The train travels as a whole along a straight path - translational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Vibrating guitar strings show which kind of motion?
questions.answer: Oscillating (vibrational) motion
questions.explanation: The strings vibrate rapidly back and forth around a resting position - oscillating motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A drill bit boring into wood shows ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: The drill bit spins rapidly around its axis while cutting - rotational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: When a rolling coin slows down and falls flat, it showed ____ before falling.
questions.answer: Both translational and rotational motion
questions.explanation: The rolling coin moved forward while spinning - a combination of both motions.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: What kind of motion does a book sliding straight across a table show?
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: Translational motion is movement in which every part of an object moves the same distance in the same direction, like a sliding book.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In translational motion, all parts of the object move ____.
choices: The same distance in the same direction
questions.answer: The same distance in the same direction
questions.explanation: Translation shifts the whole object, so every part travels the same distance and direction.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Which device mainly uses rotational motion to do its job?
questions.answer: Electric mixer
questions.explanation: An electric mixer's beaters spin around an axis - rotational motion doing the work.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which is NOT an example of rotational motion?
choices: A runner sprinting on a straight track
questions.answer: A runner sprinting on a straight track
questions.explanation: The sprinter moves straight ahead (translational); wheels, globes, and gears rotate.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: The Earth rotating once every 24 hours around its axis is ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: Earth spins around its own axis, which causes day and night - rotational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which observation proves that a wheel has rotational motion?
choices: The wheel makes a straight line
A spot painted on the rim moves in a circle
questions.answer: A spot painted on the rim moves in a circle
questions.explanation: A marked point on the rim traces a circle around the axle, proving rotation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: The Earth traveling around the Sun once a year is best described as ____.
choices: Translational (orbital) motion of the Earth as a whole
questions.answer: Translational (orbital) motion of the Earth as a whole
questions.explanation: Earth moves as a whole along its orbit around the Sun - a form of translational (orbital) motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In rotational motion, every point of the object moves around ____.
questions.answer: A fixed axis or center
questions.explanation: Rotation means all points of the object travel in circles around one fixed axis or center point.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: A confined fluid at 150 Pa pushes on a piston of area 3 m2. What force results?
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 150 Pa x 3 m2 = 450 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Excavator arms are moved by ____ applying Pascal's Principle.
questions.answer: Hydraulic cylinders
questions.explanation: Hydraulic cylinders use confined fluid under pressure to push and pull the excavator's arms with great force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A barber's hydraulic chair rises when the barber pumps the foot pedal. This demonstrates ____.
choices: Pascal's Principle in a hydraulic lift
questions.answer: Pascal's Principle in a hydraulic lift
questions.explanation: Pumping increases fluid pressure, transmitted to a large piston that lifts the chair - Pascal's Principle.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: A confined fluid at 400 Pa pushes on a piston of area 4 m2. What force results?
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 400 Pa x 4 m2 = 1600 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Which device works based on Pascal's Principle?
questions.answer: Hydraulic jack
questions.explanation: A hydraulic jack multiplies force using confined fluid pressure, exactly as Pascal's Principle describes.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A force of 180 N produces a pressure of 30 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which scientist is Pascal's Principle named after?
questions.answer: Blaise Pascal
questions.explanation: Blaise Pascal, a French mathematician and physicist, described how confined fluids transmit pressure.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: One pascal is equal to ____.
questions.answer: 1 newton per square meter
questions.explanation: By definition, 1 Pa = 1 N/m2.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: A water pressure of 40 Pa acts on a piston of area 5 m2. The force on the piston is ____.
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 40 Pa x 5 m2 = 200 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: If pressure in a confined fluid is 200 Pa and a piston has area 3 m2, what force does the fluid exert on it?
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 200 Pa x 3 m2 = 600 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.answer: Pascal (Pa)
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals; 1 Pa = 1 N/m2.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: A force of 70 N acts on an area of 10 m2. What pressure is produced?
questions.answer: 7 Pa
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Which statement about pascals is correct?
questions.answer: 1 kPa = 1000 Pa
questions.explanation: 'Kilo' means one thousand, so 1 kilopascal equals 1000 pascals.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: In a hydraulic jack, the small input piston is used to ____.
choices: Apply a small force that creates pressure in the fluid
questions.answer: Apply a small force that creates pressure in the fluid
questions.explanation: The small piston converts your modest force into fluid pressure, which the large piston turns into a big lifting force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 30 N acts on an area of 5 m2. What pressure is produced?
questions.answer: 6 Pa
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Pascal's Principle explains why pressing a toothpaste tube anywhere pushes paste out of the opening because ____.
choices: Pressure is transmitted through the confined paste in all directions
questions.answer: Pressure is transmitted through the confined paste in all directions
questions.explanation: The paste behaves as a confined fluid; squeezing anywhere transmits pressure to the nozzle.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: In Pascal's Principle, when pressure is transmitted through a confined fluid, it ____.
choices: Stays the same at every point
questions.answer: Stays the same at every point
questions.explanation: The transmitted pressure is undiminished - equal at every point in the confined fluid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Quick check: Hydraulic car brakes use Pascal's Principle to ____.
choices: Transmit brake pedal force through brake fluid to all wheels
questions.answer: Transmit brake pedal force through brake fluid to all wheels
questions.explanation: Pressing the pedal creates pressure in the brake fluid, which is transmitted equally to push brake pistons at each wheel.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: A force of 10 N on a piston of area 2 m2 creates what pressure?
questions.answer: 5 Pa
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A hydraulic press is most commonly used to ____.
choices: Compress or shape materials with large force
questions.answer: Compress or shape materials with large force
questions.explanation: Hydraulic presses use force multiplication from Pascal's Principle to compress, stamp, or shape materials.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Which action would make a clay ball that sinks start to float?
choices: Reshape it into a hollow boat shape
questions.answer: Reshape it into a hollow boat shape
questions.explanation: A hollow shape displaces much more water for the same mass, raising buoyant force until it floats.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Hot air balloons rise because ____.
choices: Helium is required in all balloons
Heated air inside is less dense than the surrounding cool air
questions.answer: Heated air inside is less dense than the surrounding cool air
questions.explanation: Hot air is less dense, so the balloon displaces cooler air weighing more than the balloon system - buoyancy lifts it.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Which object will most likely FLOAT in water?
questions.answer: A wooden block
questions.explanation: Wood is less dense than water, so the buoyant force can support it; the metal and glass objects are denser and sink.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: When a cargo ship moves from a river into the sea, it rides slightly higher because ____.
choices: Sea water is denser than fresh water
questions.answer: Sea water is denser than fresh water
questions.explanation: Denser sea water provides more buoyant force per volume, so the ship needs to displace less water and rides higher.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: The upward force that fluids exert on objects placed in them is called ____.
questions.answer: Buoyant force
questions.explanation: Buoyant force is the upward push from a fluid that opposes an object's weight.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Why is it easier to lift a heavy rock underwater than in air?
choices: Water adds strength to your arms
Water's buoyant force partly supports the rock
questions.answer: Water's buoyant force partly supports the rock
questions.explanation: The upward buoyant force offsets part of the rock's weight, so it feels lighter underwater.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Fish use a swim bladder to ____.
choices: Control buoyancy by changing their volume
questions.answer: Control buoyancy by changing their volume
questions.explanation: Adjusting gas in the swim bladder changes the fish's volume and buoyancy so it can rise, sink, or hover.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: The volume of water displaced by a fully submerged object equals ____.
questions.answer: The volume of the object
questions.explanation: A fully submerged object pushes aside (displaces) exactly its own volume of fluid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement about Archimedes' Principle is FALSE?
choices: Denser fluids give more buoyant force
Buoyant force depends on the object's color
Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid
Buoyancy works in liquids and gases
questions.answer: Buoyant force depends on the object's color
questions.explanation: Color has no effect on buoyancy; buoyant force depends on displaced fluid weight, not appearance.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall this: Which object will most likely SINK in water?
questions.answer: A metal coin
questions.explanation: The coin is denser than water, so its weight exceeds the buoyant force and it sinks.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Life jackets help people float because they ____.
choices: Add volume filled with light material, increasing buoyant force
questions.answer: Add volume filled with light material, increasing buoyant force
questions.explanation: The foam or air adds displaced volume at little weight, so buoyant force exceeds the person's weight.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: An object exactly as dense as water will ____.
questions.answer: Hover (stay suspended) in the water
questions.explanation: Equal densities mean weight and buoyant force balance at any depth.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which design lets a small piece of steel 'float'?
choices: Shaping it into a hollow bowl
questions.answer: Shaping it into a hollow bowl
questions.explanation: A hollow shape displaces more water than its weight requires, creating enough buoyant force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: A cargo ship unloads containers at port. What happens to how deep it sits?
choices: It rises because it needs to displace less water
questions.answer: It rises because it needs to displace less water
questions.explanation: Less weight means less water needs displacing, so the hull rises in the water.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A block weighs 10 N in air and reads 7 N when submerged in water. What is the buoyant force?
questions.answer: 3 N
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = weight in air - apparent weight in water = 10 N - 7 N = 3 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who first observed living cells under a microscope and called them 'animalcules'?
questions.answer: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
questions.explanation: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek built powerful microscopes and was the first to observe bacteria and other microorganisms.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Who created the first widely recognized periodic table of elements?
questions.answer: Dmitri Mendeleev
questions.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged elements by properties in 1869, even predicting undiscovered elements.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the telephone?
questions.answer: Alexander Graham Bell
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Who coined the term 'cell' after examining cork under a microscope?
questions.answer: Robert Hooke
questions.explanation: In 1665 Robert Hooke observed cork's tiny chambers and named them 'cells'.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who discovered that lightning is electricity with the famous kite experiment?
questions.answer: Benjamin Franklin
questions.explanation: Benjamin Franklin's 1752 kite experiment showed that lightning is an electrical phenomenon.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in both Physics and Chemistry for work on radioactivity?
questions.answer: Marie Curie
questions.explanation: Marie Curie won the 1903 Physics prize and the 1911 Chemistry prize for her pioneering radioactivity research.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Whose gold foil experiment revealed the atomic nucleus?
questions.answer: Ernest Rutherford
questions.explanation: Ernest Rutherford's gold foil experiment (1911) showed atoms have a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Who discovered electromagnetic induction, the principle behind generators?
questions.answer: Michael Faraday
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831 - changing magnetic fields can induce electric current.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who proposed that the planets orbit the Sun (heliocentric model) in the 1500s?
questions.answer: Nicolaus Copernicus
questions.explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus published the heliocentric model in 1543, placing the Sun at the center of planetary orbits.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Who is known as the 'Father of Modern Chemistry' for his work on elements and conservation of mass?
questions.answer: Antoine Lavoisier
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier established the law of conservation of mass and helped build modern chemistry.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Who is called the 'Father of Genetics' for his pea plant experiments?
questions.answer: Gregor Mendel
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel's pea plant experiments in the 1860s revealed the basic laws of inheritance.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who developed the alternating current (AC) electrical system?
questions.answer: Nikola Tesla
questions.explanation: Nikola Tesla championed and developed the AC system that powers homes and industries today.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In class: Who is considered the founder of modern nursing and used statistics to improve hospital care?
questions.answer: Florence Nightingale
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing and pioneered statistical graphics to reduce hospital deaths.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Think fast: Who discovered the structure of DNA along with James Watson and Maurice Wilkins?
choices: Marie Curie produced the DNA model alone
Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images were key to the discovery
questions.answer: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images were key to the discovery
questions.explanation: Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51 X-ray diffraction image was crucial evidence for the double helix model found by Watson and Crick in 1953.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which physicist discovered X-rays?
questions.answer: Wilhelm Roentgen
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and took the first X-ray photograph of his wife's hand.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: A message claims 'Doctors hate this one trick!' to get clicks. This is ____.
questions.answer: Clickbait using sensational claims
questions.explanation: Sensational unsupported claims are clickbait; check reliable sources before believing them.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Quick check: A person repeatedly gives you backhanded compliments ('nice shirt, for once'). This is meant to ____.
choices: Lower your confidence so you seek their approval
questions.answer: Lower your confidence so you seek their approval
questions.explanation: Backhanded compliments (negging) chip at self-esteem so the manipulator's approval feels more valuable.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Someone starts with a tiny request, then slowly escalates to bigger demands. This is the ____ technique.
questions.answer: Foot-in-the-door
questions.explanation: Foot-in-the-door uses small yeses to condition you for larger commitments over time.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Recall this: A person plays the victim in every story to avoid responsibility and gain sympathy. This pattern is ____.
questions.answer: Victim-playing manipulation
questions.explanation: Constant victim-playing dodges responsibility and pressures others to comply out of sympathy.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Recall this: Which habit best protects your mind from being manipulated?
choices: Asking questions like 'Why?' and 'What is the evidence?'
questions.answer: Asking questions like 'Why?' and 'What is the evidence?'
questions.explanation: Curiosity and evidence-checking are mental defenses that expose weak or dishonest claims.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Think fast: Which is TRUE about compliments from manipulators?
choices: They are always fake in every way
They are identical to honest praise
They are often strategic tools timed before requests
questions.answer: They are often strategic tools timed before requests
questions.explanation: Watch patterns: praise that reliably precedes asks is tactical, not heartfelt.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Recall this: An ad shows only success stories and hides failures and risks. This is ____.
questions.answer: Cherry-picking evidence
questions.explanation: Cherry-picking presents only favorable examples while hiding the rest, creating a misleading picture.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: A rumor spreads fear: 'If you don't act now, something terrible will happen!' This uses ____.
questions.answer: Fear appeal
questions.explanation: Fear appeals bypass careful thinking by triggering panic; verify claims before reacting.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Quick check: Why is it useful to learn the names of manipulation tactics?
choices: It lets you manipulate others better
Naming a tactic helps you spot it and respond calmly
questions.answer: Naming a tactic helps you spot it and respond calmly
questions.explanation: Recognizing and labeling tactics ('that's false urgency') activates critical thinking and reduces their power.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: In class: Which of these is an example of POSITIVE influence?
choices: A friend hiding your books so you fail
A friend pressuring you to skip class
A friend teasing you about grades
A friend encouraging you to study by studying together
questions.answer: A friend encouraging you to study by studying together
questions.explanation: Positive influence respects you and supports genuinely good choices, like shared studying.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: What should you do if you notice someone using guilt or fear to control you?
choices: Set a clear boundary and say no calmly
questions.answer: Set a clear boundary and say no calmly
questions.explanation: Calm boundaries ('I'm not comfortable with that') protect you while keeping the interaction respectful.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Recall this: An advertisement says 'Only 2 items left! Buy NOW!' to push a fast decision. Which tactic is this?
questions.answer: False urgency / scarcity pressure
questions.explanation: Creating fake urgency or scarcity rushes you into deciding before you can think carefully.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Think fast: Someone gives compliments right before asking for money. This pattern is often ____.
questions.answer: Flattery used as manipulation
questions.explanation: Flattery before a request is designed to lower your guard; judge the request on its own merits.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: A stranger offers a small free gift, then asks for a big favor you feel obliged to return. This is abuse of ____.
questions.answer: The reciprocity instinct
questions.explanation: Manipulators exploit our natural urge to return favors; a small gift should not obligate you to big favors.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Someone twists your words to attack an argument you never made. This fallacy is called ____.
questions.answer: Straw man
questions.explanation: The straw man fallacy replaces your real position with a weaker fake version that is easier to attack.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Someone says 'You're the only one who understands me' to speed intimacy. This is ____.
questions.answer: A trust-accelerating manipulation line
questions.explanation: Special-bond claims rush closeness so requests follow before you can evaluate the person.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Think fast: Someone makes you feel guilty so you will do what they want. This is called ____.
questions.answer: Guilt-tripping
questions.explanation: Guilt-tripping is an emotional manipulation tactic that uses your conscience against you instead of honest reasons.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: In class: What is 'love bombing' usually followed by in a manipulative cycle?
choices: Ending all contact immediately with no pattern
Devaluation and control once attachment forms
questions.answer: Devaluation and control once attachment forms
questions.explanation: The typical cycle is love bombing, then devaluation, then control - recognizing the pattern helps you exit early.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Someone keeps repeating a false claim until it feels true. This effect is called ____.
questions.answer: The illusory truth effect
questions.explanation: Repetition can make false statements feel true; repetition is not evidence.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Which tactic hides real costs until after you commit?
questions.answer: Bait-and-switch
questions.explanation: Bait-and-switch lures with one offer, then swaps in worse terms after commitment.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Think fast: What is a healthy boundary with negative people?
questions.answer: Limiting exposure while staying respectful
questions.explanation: Boundaries protect your energy without cruelty - you can be kind and still step back.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Which statement best describes a resilient person?
choices: They still feel pain but find ways to cope and move forward
questions.answer: They still feel pain but find ways to cope and move forward
questions.explanation: Resilience is not numbness; resilient people feel difficulties and still use healthy strategies to recover.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Recall this: A resilient person facing bullying should FIRST ____.
choices: Tell a trusted adult or authority and keep evidence
questions.answer: Tell a trusted adult or authority and keep evidence
questions.explanation: Involving trusted adults with evidence is the safe, effective path - resilience includes seeking protection.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Recall this: Which breathing technique is commonly used to calm anxiety?
choices: Slow deep breaths: inhale 4 counts, hold, exhale 6 counts
questions.answer: Slow deep breaths: inhale 4 counts, hold, exhale 6 counts
questions.explanation: Slow exhale-focused breathing activates the body's relaxation response and lowers anxiety.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Quick check: Setting small achievable goals during hard times helps because ____.
choices: Success only comes from giant goals
Small wins rebuild confidence and a sense of control
questions.answer: Small wins rebuild confidence and a sense of control
questions.explanation: Achievable goals create momentum and prove to yourself that progress is possible.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: In class: Which belief about failure supports resilience?
choices: Failure should be hidden at all costs
Failure is feedback that guides improvement
questions.answer: Failure is feedback that guides improvement
questions.explanation: Every skilled person failed repeatedly; treating failure as information fuels persistence.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Quick check: Which habit MOST supports long-term resilience?
choices: Regular sleep, exercise, and social connection
questions.answer: Regular sleep, exercise, and social connection
questions.explanation: Physical health and supportive relationships are the foundation that helps the mind handle stress.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Recall this: What is 'reframing' in coping with stress?
choices: Looking at a situation from a different, more balanced angle
questions.answer: Looking at a situation from a different, more balanced angle
questions.explanation: Reframing changes interpretation ('I failed once' instead of 'I am a failure'), which changes emotional impact.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Think fast: Self-compassion means ____.
choices: Treating yourself with the same kindness you would offer a friend
Excusing every mistake with no learning
questions.answer: Treating yourself with the same kindness you would offer a friend
questions.explanation: Self-compassion balances honesty with kindness, which research links to greater motivation and resilience.
