questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: The CPU cooler / heatsink-fan (HSF) is best described as the part that ____.
choices: Removes heat from the processor to keep it within safe temperatures
a magnetic storage device that keeps data even when the computer is off
converts AC wall power into the DC voltages the computer components need
a fast flash-based storage device with no moving parts
questions.answer: Removes heat from the processor to keep it within safe temperatures
questions.explanation: The CPU cooler / heatsink-fan (HSF) removes heat from the processor to keep it within safe temperatures.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Why should you remove jewelry and metal watches before servicing a computer?
choices: It is only a dress code
Metal can cause short circuits and conduct static or current
questions.answer: Metal can cause short circuits and conduct static or current
questions.explanation: Conductive metal items can bridge circuits, creating shorts and shock paths.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which personal protective equipment helps prevent electrostatic discharge (ESD) damage?
questions.answer: Anti-static wrist strap
questions.explanation: An anti-static wrist strap safely drains static electricity from your body to ground.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: Which practice keeps emergency exits effective?
choices: Never block exits or extinguishers with boxes or furniture
Store spares in front of exits
questions.answer: Never block exits or extinguishers with boxes or furniture
questions.explanation: Clear exits and visible extinguishers save seconds - and lives - during emergencies.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In the DMA procedure, what should you do while disassembling?
choices: Discard screws you cannot place immediately
Document and organize every removed part and screw
Mix all screws in one pile
questions.answer: Document and organize every removed part and screw
questions.explanation: Labeled parts and screws (often with photos) make correct reassembly possible.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: What does a Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS/SDS) provide?
choices: Hazard, handling, and first-aid information for chemicals
questions.answer: Hazard, handling, and first-aid information for chemicals
questions.explanation: SDS sheets tell workers exactly how to use, store, and respond to exposures for each chemical.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: What should be checked before re-connecting a serviced computer to power?
choices: Correct cable connections, no loose screws inside, and the case properly closed
Leave the case open for airflow during testing only if instructed and supervised
Connect power immediately to save time
Skip the checklist if the parts look clean
questions.answer: Correct cable connections, no loose screws inside, and the case properly closed
questions.explanation: A pre-power checklist prevents short circuits from loose metal and mis-seated cables.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which OHS practice applies to compressed gas cylinders in a shop?
choices: Lay them rolling on the floor
Store upright, secured, with valve caps on
questions.answer: Store upright, secured, with valve caps on
questions.explanation: Secured upright storage prevents cylinders from falling and becoming dangerous projectiles.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which sign warns of electrical hazard in a workshop?
choices: A yellow triangle with a lightning bolt symbol
questions.answer: A yellow triangle with a lightning bolt symbol
questions.explanation: Standard hazard signage (lightning bolt) marks areas or equipment with electrical danger.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: Which tool inspection habit prevents accidents?
choices: Repair electrical tools with tape only
Check tools for damage (cracked handles, worn bits) before each use
questions.answer: Check tools for damage (cracked handles, worn bits) before each use
questions.explanation: A quick pre-use inspection catches defects before they cause injury.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What is the safest way to carry a system unit?
choices: With both hands supporting the bottom, close to the body
questions.answer: With both hands supporting the bottom, close to the body
questions.explanation: Bottom support and a close grip prevent drops and back strain.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which cleaning agent is appropriate for external computer surfaces?
choices: Slightly damp lint-free cloth; never spray liquid directly on the machine
Kitchen detergent foam inside the case
questions.answer: Slightly damp lint-free cloth; never spray liquid directly on the machine
questions.explanation: Minimal moisture applied to the cloth (not the device) cleans safely without seeping inside.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which is correct chemical safety when using isopropyl alcohol for cleaning?
choices: Ventilate the area, keep away from sparks, and cap the bottle
Use next to an open flame
Store in a hot sunny window
questions.answer: Ventilate the area, keep away from sparks, and cap the bottle
questions.explanation: Alcohol vapors are flammable and irritating; ventilation and sealed storage are required.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: What is the correct way to lift a heavy system unit or UPS?
choices: Bend the back and lift with the spine
Bend the knees, keep the back straight, and lift with the legs
questions.answer: Bend the knees, keep the back straight, and lift with the legs
questions.explanation: Leg-lifting technique protects the spine from strain injuries.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What should you do FIRST before opening any system unit?
choices: Turn off the computer and unplug the power cord
Open the case while it is running
questions.answer: Turn off the computer and unplug the power cord
questions.explanation: Working on a live system risks electric shock and component damage; always power down and unplug first.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which is TRUE about working alone on energized equipment?
choices: Working alone is faster and safer
It should be avoided; energized work needs supervision and proper training
Supervision only matters for new buildings
questions.answer: It should be avoided; energized work needs supervision and proper training
questions.explanation: OHS best practice: never perform risky energized work unsupervised or untrained.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which practice reduces slip hazards in a computer shop?
choices: Cleaning spills immediately and using 'wet floor' signs
questions.answer: Cleaning spills immediately and using 'wet floor' signs
questions.explanation: Immediate cleanup plus warning signs prevents the most common shop injuries.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which OHS rule applies to compressed air cans?
choices: Use near open flames for visibility
Use in short bursts, keep the can upright, and work in a ventilated area
Inhale the spray to test it
questions.answer: Use in short bursts, keep the can upright, and work in a ventilated area
questions.explanation: Upright short bursts prevent propellant/liquid discharge; ventilation avoids inhaling propellant.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which is a correct OHS response to a person receiving an electric shock?
choices: Pull the person with bare hands immediately
Cut the power at the source first, then help and call for medical aid
Wait until they wake up on their own
questions.answer: Cut the power at the source first, then help and call for medical aid
questions.explanation: Touching a person still in contact with current can electrocute the rescuer; disconnect power first.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which behavior follows OHS guidelines in a computer laboratory?
choices: Eating over an open system unit
No food or drinks near the equipment
questions.answer: No food or drinks near the equipment
questions.explanation: Spills cause shorts and shocks; keeping food and drinks away is a basic lab rule.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: What is the main purpose of grounding (earthing) in a computer shop?
choices: It provides a safe path for stray current and static charge
questions.answer: It provides a safe path for stray current and static charge
questions.explanation: Grounding protects both people (shock prevention) and equipment (static discharge path).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Before touching internal components, what should a technician do to discharge static?
choices: Wear a grounded anti-static wrist strap or touch the unpainted metal case
Rub feet on carpet to build static
questions.answer: Wear a grounded anti-static wrist strap or touch the unpainted metal case
questions.explanation: Grounding yourself first prevents ESD damage to sensitive electronics.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which component is usually installed LAST in the case because of its size?
questions.answer: The video card (GPU)
questions.explanation: Long GPUs can block access to headers and drive bays, so they are typically seated after other parts.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: When installing an M.2 SSD, the correct insertion is ____.
choices: Insert upside down until it clicks
Place on top of the slot
Insert at about a 30-degree angle into the slot, then press down and screw
questions.answer: Insert at about a 30-degree angle into the slot, then press down and screw
questions.explanation: The angled insertion aligns the edge connector with the slot; pressing flat then screwing locks it.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: Which tool helps keep small screws organized during disassembly?
choices: An open toolbox bin with everything
A magnetic parts tray or labeled containers
One mixed pile in your pocket
questions.answer: A magnetic parts tray or labeled containers
questions.explanation: Sorted, labeled screws prevent lost hardware and wrong-screw damage at reassembly.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which practice protects the CPU socket pins during installation?
choices: Never touch or drop anything into the socket; keep the cover on until installation
Store the board socket-down on foam
questions.answer: Never touch or drop anything into the socket; keep the cover on until installation
questions.explanation: Bent LGA pins are a leading cause of dead boards; handle the socket area with care.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which screwdriver size is most common for PC case screws?
questions.answer: #2 Phillips
questions.explanation: A #2 Phillips fits the majority of case, PSU, and drive screws.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What is the function of the I/O shield?
choices: A metal plate that covers and grounds the rear port area of the case
questions.answer: A metal plate that covers and grounds the rear port area of the case
questions.explanation: The I/O shield protects ports, reduces EMI, and grounds the board's rear connections.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which RAM feature prevents inserting a DDR module backwards?
choices: The notch (keying slot) on the module edge
questions.answer: The notch (keying slot) on the module edge
questions.explanation: The notch matches a rib in the slot, so wrong orientation simply won't fit.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Where does the CPU 8-pin (EPS) power cable connect?
choices: The 8-pin socket near the CPU, usually at the board's top-left
questions.answer: The 8-pin socket near the CPU, usually at the board's top-left
questions.explanation: Do not confuse it with PCIe 8-pin - the EPS plug keys differently and sits by the CPU.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: The 4-pin or 8-pin connector near the CPU socket supplies power to ____.
questions.answer: The processor (CPU)
questions.explanation: This EPS/ATX12V connector feeds dedicated power to the CPU voltage regulators.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Why are case standoffs usually brass or nylon?
choices: They insulate or safely ground the board while preventing shorts
questions.answer: They insulate or safely ground the board while preventing shorts
questions.explanation: Correct standoffs keep board contacts clear of the metal tray.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which action can crack a motherboard?
choices: Tightening the CPU cooler with uneven, excessive force
Using a pea-sized thermal paste dot
questions.answer: Tightening the CPU cooler with uneven, excessive force
questions.explanation: Tighten cooler screws gradually in a cross pattern to spread pressure evenly.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: How much thermal paste is normally applied to a CPU?
choices: A small pea-sized amount in the center
A thick layer covering the entire lid
A single tiny grain of sand only
questions.answer: A small pea-sized amount in the center
questions.explanation: A pea-sized dot spreads evenly under cooler pressure; too much paste can spill and insulate instead of conduct.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What should be connected LAST when assembling a PC?
choices: The power cord (after everything else is verified)
questions.answer: The power cord (after everything else is verified)
questions.explanation: Connecting mains power last, after inspection, is the safest sequence.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What is the function of the rear case fan in a typical airflow design?
choices: Exhaust - it pulls hot air out of the case
It pushes cold air in over the GPU
questions.answer: Exhaust - it pulls hot air out of the case
questions.explanation: Standard flow: front/bottom intake, rear/top exhaust, moving cool air across hot parts.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which check confirms RAM is fully seated?
choices: Both side clips snap back into the module notches
questions.answer: Both side clips snap back into the module notches
questions.explanation: Engaged clips mean the DIMM is locked and contacts are fully mated.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which mistake can make a new build show no display?
choices: Installing one RAM stick in slot A2
Booting with the side panel on
Monitor plugged into the motherboard port while a video card is installed
questions.answer: Monitor plugged into the motherboard port while a video card is installed
questions.explanation: With a GPU installed, displays should connect to the GPU's ports, not the board's.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: When removing a stubborn expansion card, the correct approach is ____.
choices: Pry against the motherboard with a screwdriver
Pull at a steep angle hard
Release the slot clip, remove the bracket screw, and rock gently straight up
questions.answer: Release the slot clip, remove the bracket screw, and rock gently straight up
questions.explanation: Clip release plus gentle straight rocking protects both the slot and the card.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which is the correct reassembly principle after maintenance?
choices: Reverse of disassembly, verifying each connection against your notes/photos
questions.answer: Reverse of disassembly, verifying each connection against your notes/photos
questions.explanation: Systematic reverse-order reassembly restores the machine exactly as documented.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: What should you check about the CPU fan header after assembly?
choices: The fan needs a USB port
Plug it into any random header
The fan cable is plugged into the CPU_FAN header so the board monitors and powers it
questions.answer: The fan cable is plugged into the CPU_FAN header so the board monitors and powers it
questions.explanation: CPU_FAN gives the board speed/temperature control; some boards refuse to boot without it.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: When installing a CPU into an LGA socket, what should you do first?
choices: Lift the socket lever and align the notches before lowering the CPU
Press the CPU in at an angle
Apply paste to the socket pins
questions.answer: Lift the socket lever and align the notches before lowering the CPU
questions.explanation: The lever opens the load plate; alignment notches guarantee correct orientation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: Which practice prevents damaging case plastic clips during disassembly?
choices: Force panels apart with a metal blade
Check for hidden screws and release clips gently with a plastic pry tool
questions.answer: Check for hidden screws and release clips gently with a plastic pry tool
questions.explanation: Hidden screws cause most 'stuck' panels; gentle prying preserves clips.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: Which is correct about mixing old and new RAM modules?
choices: Speeds always run at the fastest
Mixing DDR3 and DDR4 is fine
Match type (DDR generation) first; mixed speeds run at the slowest module
questions.answer: Match type (DDR generation) first; mixed speeds run at the slowest module
questions.explanation: DDR generations are physically incompatible; mixed kits downclock to the lowest common speed.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: Which tool helps retrieve a dropped screw inside a case?
choices: Pouring water to float it out
Shaking the case upside down over the motherboard
A magnetic screwdriver or magnetic pickup tool
questions.answer: A magnetic screwdriver or magnetic pickup tool
questions.explanation: Magnetic pickup retrieves screws safely; loose metal inside a case risks shorts.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which screw type typically secures an M.2 SSD to the motherboard?

questions.question: What is the purpose of a PSU shroud in modern cases?

questions.answer: It hides cables/PSU and helps separate hot PSU air from component airflow
questions.explanation: Shrouds improve aesthetics and thermal separation in modern layouts.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which post-assembly habit extends component life?
choices: Placing the tower deep in a closed cabinet
Keeping vents unblocked and dust filters cleaned regularly
questions.answer: Keeping vents unblocked and dust filters cleaned regularly
questions.explanation: Cool, dust-free airflow is the simplest longevity upgrade for any PC.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

choices: Apply paste to the case tray
Install the correct I/O shield and all standoffs matching the board's holes
Skip the I/O shield for airflow
questions.answer: Install the correct I/O shield and all standoffs matching the board's holes
questions.explanation: The I/O shield and standoff pattern prepare the case to accept the board safely.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.question: Which action prevents cross-threading case screws?
choices: Tighten one screw fully before placing others
Start each screw by hand at a slight angle-free alignment, then tighten with the driver
Use the wrong-size screw and hammer it
questions.answer: Start each screw by hand at a slight angle-free alignment, then tighten with the driver
questions.explanation: Hand-starting aligns threads; final tightening should be snug, not forced.

questions.question: What marks the correct orientation when installing a CPU?
choices: The alignment triangle / pin-1 marker matching the socket's marker

choices: the brain of the computer that executes instructions and processes data
Reads and writes cds, dvds, or blu-ray discs.
the main circuit board that connects all computer components together
temporarily stores data and programs that the CPU is actively using

questions.question: Recall this: While inspecting an opened system unit, a technician reads: 'The firmware chip that stores startup instructions and hardware settings.' Which component matches this description?
questions.answer: Bios chip.
questions.explanation: The described function is performed by the BIOS chip.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: While inspecting an opened system unit, a technician reads: 'A finned metal block that absorbs and dissipates heat from a chip.' Which component matches this description?
questions.answer: Heatsink.
questions.explanation: The described function is performed by the heatsink.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which system unit component very fast memory built near or inside the CPU that holds frequently used data?
questions.answer: Cache memory.
questions.explanation: That description belongs to the cache memory.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: What is the main function of the motherboard in a system unit?
choices: the brain of the computer that executes instructions and processes data
a magnetic storage device that keeps data even when the computer is off
The main circuit board that connects all computer components together.
temporarily stores data and programs that the CPU is actively using
questions.answer: The main circuit board that connects all computer components together.
questions.explanation: The motherboard is the component that the main circuit board that connects all computer components together.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: What is the main function of the RAM (system memory) in a system unit?
choices: the brain of the computer that executes instructions and processes data
Temporarily stores data and programs that the cpu is actively using.
the main circuit board that connects all computer components together
a magnetic storage device that keeps data even when the computer is off
questions.answer: Temporarily stores data and programs that the cpu is actively using.
questions.explanation: The RAM (system memory) is the component that temporarily stores data and programs that the CPU is actively using.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: What is the main function of the thermal paste in a system unit?
choices: A compound applied between the cpu and cooler to improve heat transfer.
the main circuit board that connects all computer components together
the brain of the computer that executes instructions and processes data
temporarily stores data and programs that the CPU is actively using
questions.answer: A compound applied between the cpu and cooler to improve heat transfer.
questions.explanation: The thermal paste is the component that a compound applied between the CPU and cooler to improve heat transfer.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: The RAM (system memory) is best described as the part that ____.
choices: renders images, video, and graphics and sends them to the monitor
a fast flash-based storage device with no moving parts
converts AC wall power into the DC voltages the computer components need
Temporarily stores data and programs that the cpu is actively using
questions.answer: Temporarily stores data and programs that the cpu is actively using
questions.explanation: The RAM (system memory) temporarily stores data and programs that the CPU is actively using.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: The hard disk drive (HDD) is best described as the part that ____.
choices: a fast flash-based storage device with no moving parts
converts AC wall power into the DC voltages the computer components need
A magnetic storage device that keeps data even when the computer is off
renders images, video, and graphics and sends them to the monitor
questions.answer: A magnetic storage device that keeps data even when the computer is off
questions.explanation: The hard disk drive (HDD) a magnetic storage device that keeps data even when the computer is off.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: While inspecting an opened system unit, a technician reads: 'Processes audio so the computer can output sound through speakers or headphones.' Which component matches this description?
questions.answer: Sound card.
questions.explanation: The described function is performed by the sound card.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: Which fire extinguisher type is used for electrical fires?
choices: Class A paper-only extinguisher filled with water
questions.answer: Class C (or CO2-type) extinguisher
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity and can electrocute the user; CO2/Class C extinguishers are rated for energized electrical fires.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which is an ergonomic practice for computer work?
choices: Position the monitor at eye level and keep wrists straight while typing
Stare at a screen placed on the floor
questions.answer: Position the monitor at eye level and keep wrists straight while typing
questions.explanation: Ergonomics reduces eye strain and repetitive stress injuries during long sessions.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What does 'housekeeping' mean under OHS in a computer shop?
choices: Keeping the work area clean, organized, and free of hazards
questions.answer: Keeping the work area clean, organized, and free of hazards
questions.explanation: Good housekeeping removes trip hazards, dust buildup, and clutter that cause accidents.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Why is static electricity dangerous to computer parts?
choices: It only affects the case paint
It can silently damage sensitive chips and circuits
questions.answer: It can silently damage sensitive chips and circuits
questions.explanation: ESD of even a few hundred volts can destroy microchips, often without visible signs.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: Which maintenance task helps prevent a system unit from overheating?
choices: Cleaning dust from fans, heatsinks, and vents
questions.answer: Cleaning dust from fans, heatsinks, and vents
questions.explanation: Dust insulates heat and blocks airflow; regular cleaning keeps cooling efficient.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which statement about PPE is correct?
choices: PPE replaces all other safety steps
PPE is optional if you are careful
PPE is the last line of defense after removing or controlling the hazard
questions.answer: PPE is the last line of defense after removing or controlling the hazard
questions.explanation: The hierarchy of controls: eliminate, substitute, engineer, administer - then PPE.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In a computer laboratory, OHS stands for ____.
questions.answer: Occupational Health and Safety
questions.explanation: OHS guidelines protect people from hazards while working with computers and tools.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which storage practice follows OHS guidelines?
choices: Store heavy boxes low and keep aisles clear
Block the fire exit with spare parts
Stack heavy items on top shelves
questions.answer: Store heavy boxes low and keep aisles clear
questions.explanation: Low heavy storage prevents falling-object injuries; clear aisles keep evacuation routes usable.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which is the correct DMA sequence?
questions.answer: Disassemble -> Maintain -> Assemble
questions.explanation: Work flows from safe disassembly, through maintenance/cleaning, to careful reassembly and testing.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which first-aid item must a computer shop keep stocked for cuts from sheet-metal cases?
choices: Bandages and antiseptic in the first-aid kit
questions.answer: Bandages and antiseptic in the first-aid kit
questions.explanation: Case edges cause common minor cuts; stocked first aid enables immediate care.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which tool is appropriate for blowing dust out of a system unit?
choices: Wet cloth dripping inside the case
A household vacuum pressed against chips
Compressed air / blower used in short bursts
questions.answer: Compressed air / blower used in short bursts
questions.explanation: Compressed air dislodges dust safely; vacuums can generate static and moisture causes shorts.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which behavior violates electrical OHS in a lab?
choices: Daisy-chaining multiple extension cords to reach an outlet
Replacing a short cord with a longer rated one
Using one properly rated power strip
Plugging directly into a wall outlet
questions.answer: Daisy-chaining multiple extension cords to reach an outlet
questions.explanation: Chained cords overheat and fail; use a single properly rated cord or relocate equipment.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which action reduces the risk of repetitive strain during servicing work?
choices: Taking short breaks and varying tasks/posture
questions.answer: Taking short breaks and varying tasks/posture
questions.explanation: Micro-breaks and posture changes protect muscles and joints during repetitive work.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What is the correct action when a safety guard is missing from a machine?
choices: Stop using the machine and report it before continuing
Let the fastest worker use it
questions.answer: Stop using the machine and report it before continuing
questions.explanation: Missing guards expose workers to moving parts; machines stay out of service until fixed.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: When cleaning inside a system unit, why should fans be held still while using compressed air?
choices: Fans will fly out of the case
Holding them makes cleaning slower only
Spinning fans from airflow can generate voltage and damage fan bearings or circuits
questions.answer: Spinning fans from airflow can generate voltage and damage fan bearings or circuits
questions.explanation: Letting compressed air overspin a fan can induce current back into the board and wear the bearing.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: In DMA documentation, what does 'labeling cables before removal' prevent?
choices: Wrong reconnections that can damage components or stop the system from booting
questions.answer: Wrong reconnections that can damage components or stop the system from booting
questions.explanation: Labels (or photos) ensure each cable returns to its exact original header or port.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: A classmate spills water near a powered computer. The correct OHS action is ____.
choices: Use a hair dryer on high heat inside the case
Wipe quickly while the PC stays on
Ignore it if the PC still runs
Shut down and unplug the unit, then dry and inspect before powering again
questions.answer: Shut down and unplug the unit, then dry and inspect before powering again
questions.explanation: Water plus electricity equals shock and short risk; power down, dry thoroughly, and inspect first.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: During an earthquake in a computer laboratory, the OHS priority is ____.
choices: Protect people first - drop, cover, hold; secure equipment afterwards
questions.answer: Protect people first - drop, cover, hold; secure equipment afterwards
questions.explanation: Human safety always comes before equipment; follow evacuation procedures after the shaking stops.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: A worker notices a frayed (damaged) power cord. What is the correct OHS action?
choices: Stop using it, tag it as defective, and report it for replacement
Wrap it with paper and continue
Use it only on busy days
questions.answer: Stop using it, tag it as defective, and report it for replacement
questions.explanation: Damaged cords are shock and fire hazards; defective equipment must be tagged and removed from service.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: If a component does not seat properly during assembly, you should ____.
choices: Stop and check alignment; never force the part
questions.answer: Stop and check alignment; never force the part
questions.explanation: Forcing parts breaks connectors and boards; misalignment is the usual cause of resistance.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: A technician finds a swollen capacitor on a motherboard during maintenance. The correct action is ____.
choices: Continue using it until it pops
Do not use the board; report/replace it, as swollen capacitors can fail or leak
Press the capacitor back into shape
questions.answer: Do not use the board; report/replace it, as swollen capacitors can fail or leak
questions.explanation: Swollen capacitors indicate failing components and possible leakage; the board needs repair or replacement.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which sign shows a power supply is correctly oriented in the case?
choices: Its fan faces the case vent (usually down with a bottom vent) for proper airflow
questions.answer: Its fan faces the case vent (usually down with a bottom vent) for proper airflow
questions.explanation: The PSU fan should draw air from a vent; blocked fans cause overheating and shutdowns.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which best practice applies to keeping track of disassembly steps?
choices: Remove everything as fast as possible
Take photos of cable routes and part positions before removing anything
questions.answer: Take photos of cable routes and part positions before removing anything
questions.explanation: Photos are fast, reliable documentation for correct reassembly.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which component should be installed into the motherboard BEFORE mounting the motherboard in the case (common practice)?
choices: The CPU (and often RAM and M.2 SSD)
questions.answer: The CPU (and often RAM and M.2 SSD)
questions.explanation: CPU, RAM, and M.2 drives are far easier to seat with the board on a flat surface outside the case.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which cable powers most modern SATA hard drives and SSDs?
choices: The SATA power connector from the power supply
questions.answer: The SATA power connector from the power supply
questions.explanation: SATA drives need both a SATA data cable (to motherboard) and a SATA power cable (from PSU).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Quick check: How should RAM modules be removed from their slots?
choices: Press the slot clips outward, then lift the module straight up
questions.answer: Press the slot clips outward, then lift the module straight up
questions.explanation: Releasing the retention clips lets the DIMM lift out cleanly without bending pins or traces.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which action during disassembly risks data loss?
choices: Removing or dropping a spinning hard drive while it is powered
questions.answer: Removing or dropping a spinning hard drive while it is powered
questions.explanation: Powering-off before handling drives prevents head crashes and data corruption.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: What does the 'PWR_SW' front-panel cable do?
choices: Connects the case power button to the motherboard so it can turn the system on
questions.answer: Connects the case power button to the motherboard so it can turn the system on
questions.explanation: Polarity usually doesn't matter for switches; see the manual for the exact header pins.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which action avoids static buildup while assembling on carpet?
choices: Work on a hard floor with an anti-static mat; avoid carpet entirely
questions.answer: Work on a hard floor with an anti-static mat; avoid carpet entirely
questions.explanation: Carpet generates static; hard surfaces with grounded mats are the safe workspace.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which cable provides main power to the motherboard?
questions.answer: The 24-pin ATX power connector
questions.explanation: The large 24-pin connector from the PSU delivers the motherboard's main power rails.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: When removing the CPU cooler, why should you clean off old thermal paste?
choices: Old paste dries out and loses heat-transfer ability
questions.answer: Old paste dries out and loses heat-transfer ability
questions.explanation: Fresh thermal paste applied at reassembly ensures efficient heat transfer from CPU to cooler.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which component requires alignment with the I/O shield ports at the rear of the case?
questions.answer: The motherboard
questions.explanation: The board's rear ports must line up with the I/O shield openings as it is seated.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which motherboard connector powers case cooling fans?
questions.answer: The 3-pin or 4-pin SYS_FAN / CHA_FAN headers
questions.explanation: Fan headers supply power and (4-pin) speed control for chassis fans.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: Why should you avoid over-tightening motherboard screws?
choices: Excess force can crack the board or strip threads
questions.answer: Excess force can crack the board or strip threads
questions.explanation: Snug is enough; PCB layers and standoffs can crack under excessive torque.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which is correct for installing a 2.5-inch SSD in a desktop case?
choices: Glue it to the case floor
Mount it in a 2.5-inch bay or adapter, then connect SATA data and power
Install it inside the PSU shroud loose
questions.answer: Mount it in a 2.5-inch bay or adapter, then connect SATA data and power
questions.explanation: Secure mounting plus both cables (data + power) completes the installation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Why should you test-boot a new build before final cable management?
choices: To catch problems while every component is still easy to reach
Cable management must come first always
It is only for used parts
questions.answer: To catch problems while every component is still easy to reach
questions.explanation: Fixing a no-POST build is far easier before everything is zip-tied and tucked.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Which screwdriver type is most commonly used for PC case and component screws?
questions.answer: Phillips (cross-head) screwdriver
questions.explanation: Most PC screws use Phillips heads, making a Phillips screwdriver the essential PC tool.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What is the purpose of the small lever on a SATA connector?
choices: It locks the cable so it does not slip out
questions.answer: It locks the cable so it does not slip out
questions.explanation: Press the metal/plastic latch when removing; forcing it breaks the lock.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: After assembling a new PC, it does not power on. Which checks come FIRST?
choices: Power switch on PSU, wall outlet live, 24-pin and CPU power seated, front-panel PWR_SW correct
questions.answer: Power switch on PSU, wall outlet live, 24-pin and CPU power seated, front-panel PWR_SW correct
questions.explanation: Power-path checks (PSU switch, cables, power-button header) resolve most no-boot assemblies.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: What is the purpose of the small front-panel cables (PWR_SW, RESET_SW, HDD_LED)?
choices: They connect case buttons and indicator lights to motherboard headers
questions.answer: They connect case buttons and indicator lights to motherboard headers
questions.explanation: These tiny labeled cables must match the motherboard's front-panel header layout.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: When disconnecting a 24-pin ATX connector, the correct technique is ____.
choices: Press the release latch and rock the connector gently straight out
questions.answer: Press the release latch and rock the connector gently straight out
questions.explanation: The latch holds the connector; rocking releases it without stressing pins or wires.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Why should dual-channel RAM be installed in matching-color slots?
choices: It reduces power use to zero
It enables dual-channel mode for better memory performance
questions.answer: It enables dual-channel mode for better memory performance
questions.explanation: Matching slots (per the manual) pair the modules for dual-channel bandwidth.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: When seating an expansion card (like a video card), the correct method is ____.
choices: Rock it side to side violently
Align with the slot and press firmly straight down until the retention clip engages
questions.answer: Align with the slot and press firmly straight down until the retention clip engages
questions.explanation: Straight, even pressure seats all slot pins; the clip and bracket screw then secure it.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What does a long single beep (or beep code) at power-on usually indicate?
choices: A hardware issue reported by POST (meaning varies by BIOS brand)
questions.answer: A hardware issue reported by POST (meaning varies by BIOS brand)
questions.explanation: Consult the motherboard manual's beep-code table to identify the failing part.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which practice protects a motherboard during assembly outside the case?
choices: Place it on its anti-static bag on a flat, non-conductive surface
Balance it on a screwdriver box
Rest it on the metal case top
questions.answer: Place it on its anti-static bag on a flat, non-conductive surface
questions.explanation: The bag is static-safe; metal surfaces can short the board's underside solder points.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In class: Which step confirms a disassembled drive's data cable connection?
choices: The SATA data cable is clicked into both the drive and a motherboard SATA port
The cable is coiled inside the case
The cable is plugged into the PSU
The cable is loosely resting on the drive
questions.answer: The SATA data cable is clicked into both the drive and a motherboard SATA port
questions.explanation: SATA data connections click at both ends; loose cables cause drives to disappear from the system.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Think fast: Why are standoffs installed between the case and motherboard?
choices: They create space so the motherboard's solder points do not touch and short on the metal case
questions.answer: They create space so the motherboard's solder points do not touch and short on the metal case
questions.explanation: Standoffs raise the board and align it with case screw holes, preventing shorts.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall this: Which step prevents a video card from sagging and stressing its slot?
choices: Tape it to the side panel
Secure the bracket screw (and a support bracket for heavy cards)
questions.answer: Secure the bracket screw (and a support bracket for heavy cards)
questions.explanation: The bracket screw anchors the card; heavy GPUs benefit from support brackets.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: When removing a heat-sink assembly stuck to a CPU, the safe approach is ____.
choices: Gently twist the cooler to break the paste bond before lifting
questions.answer: Gently twist the cooler to break the paste bond before lifting
questions.explanation: A gentle twist separates the bonded paste; yanking can pull the CPU out of its socket and bend pins.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What is the correct order to start disassembling a desktop computer?
choices: Power off, unplug all cables, then open the case
Remove the CPU first while powered
questions.answer: Power off, unplug all cables, then open the case
questions.explanation: Safe disassembly always begins with complete power removal and cable disconnection.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: In BIOS/UEFI setup, what is the purpose of the integrated graphics selection?
choices: keeps the computer's clock accurate for files, logs, and certificates
restricts access to the firmware setup so unauthorized users cannot change settings
sets the order of devices the computer searches for an operating system at startup
It chooses whether video output comes from the cpu's graphics or a separate video card.
questions.answer: It chooses whether video output comes from the cpu's graphics or a separate video card.
questions.explanation: The integrated graphics selection chooses whether video output comes from the CPU's graphics or a separate video card.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Which BIOS/UEFI feature sets how the firmware talks to storage drives, affecting performance and features?
questions.answer: Sata mode (ahci).
questions.explanation: That function belongs to the SATA mode (AHCI) setting.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Which BIOS/UEFI feature allows a powered-off PC to be turned on by a network signal?
questions.answer: Wake-on-lan setting.
questions.explanation: That function belongs to the Wake-on-LAN setting setting.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Quick check: A technician needs a firmware feature that allows a powered-off PC to be turned on by a network signal. Which setting should be used?
questions.answer: Wake-on-lan setting.
questions.explanation: The Wake-on-LAN setting provides exactly that function.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Think fast: The UEFI graphical interface in firmware setup is best described as the option that ____.
choices: checks digital signatures during boot so only trusted software loads
The modern firmware ui that supports mouse control, higher resolutions, and faster booting
allows one physical machine to run virtual machines efficiently
turns built-in components like audio or network adapters on or off
questions.answer: The modern firmware ui that supports mouse control, higher resolutions, and faster booting
questions.explanation: The UEFI graphical interface the modern firmware UI that supports mouse control, higher resolutions, and faster booting.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: In class: In BIOS/UEFI setup, what is the purpose of the Load Optimized Defaults option?
choices: restricts access to the firmware setup so unauthorized users cannot change settings
It restores all firmware settings to safe factory values.
sets the order of devices the computer searches for an operating system at startup
keeps the computer's clock accurate for files, logs, and certificates
questions.answer: It restores all firmware settings to safe factory values.
questions.explanation: The Load Optimized Defaults option restores all firmware settings to safe factory values.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: The setup entry key (Del, F2, etc.) in firmware setup is best described as the option that ____.
choices: allows one physical machine to run virtual machines efficiently
checks digital signatures during boot so only trusted software loads
turns built-in components like audio or network adapters on or off
The key pressed during startup to open the firmware settings screen
questions.answer: The key pressed during startup to open the firmware settings screen
questions.explanation: The setup entry key (Del, F2, etc.) the key pressed during startup to open the firmware settings screen.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: In class: Which BIOS/UEFI feature powers the memory that keeps BIOS settings and clock when the PC is unplugged?
questions.answer: Cmos battery.
questions.explanation: That function belongs to the CMOS battery setting.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Which BIOS/UEFI feature restores all firmware settings to safe factory values?
questions.answer: Load optimized defaults option.
questions.explanation: That function belongs to the Load Optimized Defaults option setting.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Recall this: In BIOS/UEFI setup, what is the purpose of the Secure Boot?
choices: It checks digital signatures during boot so only trusted software loads.
keeps the computer's clock accurate for files, logs, and certificates
sets the order of devices the computer searches for an operating system at startup
restricts access to the firmware setup so unauthorized users cannot change settings
questions.answer: It checks digital signatures during boot so only trusted software loads.
questions.explanation: The Secure Boot checks digital signatures during boot so only trusted software loads.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Which BIOS/UEFI feature the modern firmware UI that supports mouse control, higher resolutions, and faster booting?
questions.answer: Uefi graphical interface.
questions.explanation: That function belongs to the UEFI graphical interface setting.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Recall this: The integrated graphics selection in firmware setup is best described as the option that ____.
choices: Chooses whether video output comes from the cpu's graphics or a separate video card
turns built-in components like audio or network adapters on or off
checks digital signatures during boot so only trusted software loads
allows one physical machine to run virtual machines efficiently
questions.answer: Chooses whether video output comes from the cpu's graphics or a separate video card
questions.explanation: The integrated graphics selection chooses whether video output comes from the CPU's graphics or a separate video card.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: A technician needs a firmware feature that the modern firmware UI that supports mouse control, higher resolutions, and faster booting. Which setting should be used?
questions.answer: Uefi graphical interface.
questions.explanation: The UEFI graphical interface provides exactly that function.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 2
questions.question: Which BIOS/UEFI feature the startup routine that checks essential hardware before the OS loads?

The physical serial of the device

questions.explanation: IP addresses locate devices logically so data can be routed to them.

questions.answer: Repeater
questions.explanation: Repeaters amplify/rebuild signals so networks can span longer distances.

questions.answer: Router

questions.answer: Administrator account

Move them to the Recycle Bin
Back them up to external storage or cloud

questions.explanation: A clean install erases the system partition; backups are the only protection.

questions.answer: Device drivers (chipset, video, network)
questions.explanation: Drivers make hardware work fully; Windows Update then supplies the rest.

questions.explanation: 64 GB is the official minimum device storage for Windows 11.

It tags your name for grades

questions.explanation: Lockout/tagout ensures nobody re-energizes equipment mid-service - a core safety standard.

choices: Shut it down, unplug everything, and secure loose internal components if needed
Carry it while running on battery
